agent.problem: Six of the ten choice cards require unrevealed facts to be guessed: cards 2, 4, 5, 10, 15 and 18 ask who brings the case, why the leaders want Paul summoned, how Festus responds, whether the charges can be proved, what Festus knows and how Festus answers the appeal without enough earlier context to reason out the answers. Discovery questions therefore outnumber the informed guesses instead of being just a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The distractor "Before the magistrates of Tarsus" is not a real detail from somewhere in the Bible. Tarsus appears in Scripture, but magistrates of Tarsus do not, so this where-question needs a different biblical distractor.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

agent.problem: The baker has no basis from the earlier cards for choosing "knows" rather than "doubts" or "denies." The blank asks for unrevealed wording from verse 10 instead of testing a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
